 Bowling Alley, Tennis Court, Car Gallery: AI Imagines A $55 Million Home In The DC Area 
 November 10th
 by UrbanTurf Staff 
 ✉️ Want to forward this article? Click here .
 Conceptual image of the exterior. Click to enlarge. 
 The DC area’s priciest yet-to-be-built home is back on the market, and this time artificial intelligence is doing the selling. 
 7020 Green Oak Drive in McLean returned to the market this week with a $55 million asking price, up $5 million from when UrbanTurf last covered the property in 2024. Listed with Fouad Talout and John Spahr of Long & Foster, the planned 30,000-square-foot residence would sit on a five-acre lot with about 425 feet of Potomac River frontage. However, since the home has not been built, the listing is relying on AI-generated images to show what the finished estate could look like. 
 Click to enlarge. 
 The images leave little to the imagination. A pair of sports cars sits in a motor court in front of a wood-and-glass entry, and a double-height great room features a cascading chandelier, a floating staircase and a shot looking out at the Potomac River. Elsewhere, the images show an indoor tennis court with a glass-walled lounge overlooking it, and a lap pool adjacent to a bowling alley. There’s also a garage-turned-gallery holding more than a dozen classic and exotic cars, two motorcycles and walls of racing trophies and helmets, plus an infinity pool spilling toward a sunset river view.  
 Indoor pool and bowling alley. Click to enlarge. 
 The images line up with the amenities in the listing description, including indoor and outdoor pools, a tennis court, a bowling alley, an 18-car garage and parking for more than 70 vehicles.  
 Garage. Click to enlarge. 
 The listing has cycled on and off the market several times since early 2023, and the description notes that the riverfront parcel is also available for purchase as land only. If the home is ever built and sells near its asking price, it would shatter the record for the most expensive home sale in the DC region. For now, it exists mostly in the imagination of an algorithm.
